content: 1. Nirmatrelvir, a substrate of the CYP3A4 enzyme, is contraindicated for use with strong CYP3A4 inducers. This is because strong inducers can significantly reduce plasma concentrations of nirmatrelvir, potentially leading to a loss of virologic response and the development of resistance. Initiation of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir therapy should not occur immediately after discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inducer due to the time required for systemic clearance of the inducer. 2. Rifampin, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, decreases the plasma levels and efficacy of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir by enhancing the metabolism of the drug through hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. This interaction is contraindicated. 3. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels of niragestat, nisoldipine, and nitrendipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered, and close monitoring is advised for nitrendipine. 4. Rifampin decreases norethindrone levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and alternative or backup contraception is recommended. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised, as coadministration may increase menstrual-related adverse effects such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, and menorrhagia. 5. Rifampin reduces the levels of norethindrone acetate and norethindrone transdermal formulations by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during coadministration, and alternative contraception methods are recommended. 6. Rifampin decreases the levels of norgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Patients should use alternative or backup contraception during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inducer. 7. Rifampin reduces the levels of olanzapine and olanzapine/samidorphan by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism, decreasing their efficacy. Strong CYP3A4 inducers reduce olanzapine levels by ~50% and samidorphan levels by ~75%. Alternative drugs are recommended. 8. Rifampin decreases the levels of olaparib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 9. Rifampin reduces the levels of oliceridine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the oliceridine dose and monitor for respiratory depression. 10. Rifampin decreases the levels of olutasidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its efficacy. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 11. Rifampin reduces the levels of omaveloxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. 12. Rifampin decreases the levels of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing their efficacy. This interaction is contraindicated. 13. Rifampin reduces the levels of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs or close monitoring is recommended. 14. Rifampin decreases the levels of ondansetron by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 15. Rifampin reduces the levels of opium tincture by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Rifampin decreases the levels of osilodrostat by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended during coadministration and after discontinuation of strong inducers. 17. Rifampin reduces the levels of osimertinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 18. Rifampin decreases the levels of ospemifene by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 19. Rifampin reduces the levels of oxacillin by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Rifampin decreases the levels of oxybutynin and oxycodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 21. Rifampin reduces the levels of ozanimod by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism, decreasing the exposure of its active metabolites (CC112273 and CC1084037). Coadministration with strong CYP2C8 inducers is not recommended. 22. Rifampin decreases the levels of paclitaxel and paclitaxel protein-bound formulations by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 metabolism and by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Close monitoring is recommended. 23. Rifampin reduces the levels of palbociclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, decreasing plasma exposure by ~85%. Alternative drugs are recommended. 24. Rifampin decreases the levels of paliperidone by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Dose adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 25. Rifampin reduces the levels of palovarotene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 26. Rifampin decreases the levels of panobinostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its efficacy by ~70%. This interaction is contraindicated. 27. Rifampin reduces the levels of pantoprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 28. Rifampin decreases the levels of parecoxib by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 29. Rifampin reduces the levels of paromomycin by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Close monitoring is recommended. 30. Rifampin decreases the levels of pazopanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 31. Rifampin reduces the levels of pemigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 32. Rifampin decreases the levels of pentobarbital by increasing its metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 33. Rifampin reduces the levels of perampanel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be necessary during coadministration. 34. Rifampin decreases the levels of perindopril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Rifampin increases the levels of pexidartinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and gastrointestinal absorption. Coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors requires dose adjustments. Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity, and coadministration with other hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. 36. Rifampin reduces the levels of phenobarbital by increasing its metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 37. Rifampin decreases the levels of phenytoin by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 38. Rifampin reduces the levels of pimavanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be necessary, and coadministration should be avoided if possible. 39. Rifampin decreases the levels of pimozide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 40. Rifampin reduces the levels of pioglitazone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 41. Rifampin decreases the levels of pirfenidone by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Strong CYP1A2 inducers should be discontinued before initiating pirfenidone therapy. 42. Rifampin reduces the levels of pimenol and piroxicam by increasing their metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 43. Rifampin decreases the levels of pirtobrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 44. Rifampin increases the levels of pitavastatin by decreasing its metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Alternative drugs are recommended. 45. Rifampin reduces the levels of pitolisant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, decreasing exposure by ~50%. Dose adjustments are necessary during coadministration. 46. Rifampin decreases the levels of polatuzumab vedotin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the exposure of unconjugated MMAE. Close monitoring is recommended. 47. Rifampin reduces the levels of pomalidomide by inducing CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended.
